rows.grounds: Accusative singular qualifier describing the object obtained; agrees with santānikaṃ.
Accusative singular object of labdhvā; denotes a rite or observance connected with lineage/continuity in this context.
Absolutive expressing prior action leading to the result stated by iṣṭadam.
Compound indicating purpose: pitṛ (ancestors) + deva (gods) + artha (purpose).
Compound qualifier of santānikaṃ: iṣṭa (desired) + da (giving); indicates the rite yields desired results.

items.question: What Śaiva lineage rite fulfills the desires of ancestors and gods?
premises: A Śaiva lineage rite can be obtained.
This rite is performed for ancestors and gods.
The rite grants what is desired.
items.inference: Therefore, obtaining and performing the Śaiva lineage rite for ancestors and gods fulfills their desires.
uncertainties: The precise ritual referent of santānikaṃ in this Śaiva context is not fully specified.
items.plain_english: Having obtained the Śaiva lineage rite for the sake of the ancestors and the gods, one gains what is desired.
